annotation.title_clean: Opening Speech by Second Minister for Transport Ng Chee Meng for the Road Traffic (Amendment) Bill Second Reading
annotation.title_en: Opening Speech by Second Minister for Transport Ng Chee Meng for the Road Traffic (Amendment) Bill Second Reading
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Ministry of Transport, Singapore (Ng Chee Meng, Second Minister for Transport)
named_instruments_referenced: Motor Vehicles (Third-Party Risk and Compensation) Act
annotation.summary_en: Singapore Second Minister for Transport's second-reading speech introducing the Road Traffic (Amendment) Bill 2017. The bill lets the Minister make rules for autonomous vehicle trials (SAE levels 3-5) under a five-year regulatory sandbox, exempting AVs from rules that assume a human driver. It also regulates private-hire car services and raises penalties, taking a light-touch approach that puts safety first.
key_provisions_or_claims: Clause 6 empowers the Minister to make rules on AV trials and use: time and space limits, design standards for AV equipment, and requirements to share trial data
Covers SAE J3016 levels 3, 4 and 5 automation but not driver-assistance systems
AVs and trial operators can be exempted from Road Traffic Act provisions that assume a human driver is responsible
The regulatory sandbox is limited to five years, after which permanent legislation will be considered
Government will run programmes to help professional drivers retrain for an AV world
